Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary assessment findings:
  - Acute allergic reaction to wasp sting with bronchospasm and cutaneous signs (blotchy rash) occurring within minutes of sting
  - Perioral lip tingling reported; throat tightness sensation but no documented throat edema
  - Wheeze and chest tightness with shallow breathing
  - No documented hypotension or explicit airway obstruction at presentation
  - Background history of eczema; penicillin allergy
  - Home antihistamines available; patient advised ambulance due to potential anaphylaxis
- Integrating DDx considerations:
  - Likely: Anaphylaxis to wasp sting (High) given rapid onset after sting, airway/breathing symptoms, and skin changes
  - Possible: Wasp venom–induced allergic reaction with bronchospasm (Medium)
  - Possible: Panic/anxiety-driven hyperventilation with paresthesias (Medium)
  - Note: No conflict between transcript and DDx; no contradictory data identified

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Anaphylaxis to wasp sting
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Rapid onset after sting; lip tingling; wheeze; chest tightness; blotchy rash
- Wasp venom–induced allergic reaction with bronchospasm (systemic allergic reaction without established shock)
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Bronchospasm and rash after sting; could represent evolving reaction
- Panic/anxiety-driven hyperventilation with associated paresthesias
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Acute dyspnea with perioral tingling after distressing event; however allergic etiology more likely given timeline and signs
